title: Working Out the Run of an Approval on a Ridgecrest RxSecure Drug Coverage Request
content:
The run for which an approval on a drug coverage request under a Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan holds good is worked out in whole days from the day the decision is given.

## The order of the working

The plan starts from the term the request itself earns, counts that term on the basis the member's fill history gives, takes off the allowance a standing denial earns, adds the allowance the pharmacy channel earns, takes off the days already elapsed from the day the run is anchored to, takes off the allowance the plan's quantity limits earn, and never issues a run shorter than the plan's floor. The subtractions and the addition are made in that order on the counted term, and the floor is compared only with the figure they leave.

## The quantities that enter it

- The term the request earns is the plan's ordinary term of 180 days.
- The counted term is the term the request earns, counted as booked.
- No allowance is taken off for a standing denial.
- No allowance is added for the pharmacy channel.
- The run is anchored to the day the decision is given, so no days are taken off as already elapsed.
- No allowance is taken off for quantity limits.
- The plan's floor is 30 days.

## Worked through

Starting from the term the request earns, 180 days, counted as booked, 180 days stands. Taking off nothing for a standing denial leaves 180 days; adding nothing for the pharmacy channel leaves 180 days; taking off no elapsed days leaves 180 days; taking off nothing for quantity limits leaves 180 days. That figure is then compared with the floor of 30 days, and being the greater it governs, so the approval is issued for a run of 180 days.

Were the same working to leave a figure below 30 days, the floor would govern and the run issued would be 30 days.

A request the prescriber has asked to have expedited is always expedited, and the run a decision earns is never shortened because the member rather than the prescriber asked for the drug.
